Why is a server required? Couldn't I just crypto-communicate with someone using only the two devices involved?
Is there something similar to Signal (by Open Whisper Systems) that doesn't rely on some server?

Right now, Tox is probably the closest thing. But the Android client is still alpha & does not support video yet.

Another option is Silence; it forked from Signal back when Signal was multiple apps (it forked the TextSecure app). It only supports texting but actually works over SMS rather than requiring data. (Note that that means the metadata is still vulnerable.)

For those of you that don't know: F-Droid is basically a Play Store but with almost all open source and free software. The best part is this repo and package manager /updater will display the license of apps next to their names. To install it you have to go to Security in your Settings and allow installation of apps from sources other than the Play Store. Then visit https://f-droid.org/ and download it. You can install it after opening it by clicking on the downloaded FDroid.apk file in your downloads.

If you want to get Antox (the Android client for Tox), you can download the Antox APK file but it looks like you won't get updates to Antox this way. Get it through F-Droid by adding the Tox repository https://pkg.tox.chat/fdroid/repo to F-Droid, this will keep it updated. This step is unnecessary for most apps which are already available on F-Droid.

I'm not entirely sure because I haven't used it much (I've only got one friend on it so far) but I think that text will be sent. Images cannot be sent unless the recipient is online (at least on Antox).

Also, all the apps in the default repositories are free and open source software. There are a few other repos that offer non-FOSS apps but I've only found a couple.

There is also an alpha app, the F-Droid privileged extension, that aims to let you install apps without turning on 3rd party installs but I can't get it to work on my phone yet. I used to be able to install F-Droid as a system app to get the and effect, but I can't figure out how since Android 5.

If you want, take a look at v/flossdroid, a sub for FLOSS on Android.
